meta.title: The Paw Print on the Flag
meta.textType: story: a picture story with a main idea

paragraphs: On Saturday, June sixth, the Explorers needed a flag. Leo wanted to design the flag himself. At ten o'clock, he came to Lily's garden with a big green cloth. He also brought a pot of white paint and a brush. Lily and Mia sat on the grass and watched him. The cloth was clean and dry. "I want to paint a white leaf in the middle," said Leo. "A leaf is a nice design," said Mia.

"Wait here, please," said Leo. "I need a drink first." He left the pot and the brush beside the cloth and went into the house. Pip played near the gate with his red ball. Then the ball went across the grass. Pip was running after his red ball when he stepped in the pot of paint. His front paws were white and wet. "Pip!" shouted Lily. Leo was coming back with a cup of water when Pip suddenly jumped on the cloth. Pip landed in the middle, left one big white paw print, and ran after his ball. "Oh no!" said Leo in surprise. He dropped the cup on the grass. "Who did this?"

Pip came back and sat on the grass with the ball. His white paws were still wet. Lily and Mia began to laugh. "It looks like a paw print," said Lily. "Pip made a special sign for the club by accident!" "A paw print on a green flag is perfect," said Mia. Leo looked at the big white paw print for a long time. Then he began to smile. "A paw print is better than a leaf," he said. Leo decided to keep it. They waited in the sun for an hour. Lily's brother Tom came out of the house with a long stick. "Is the paint dry?" he asked. Leo touched the paw print with one finger. "Yes, it is dry now," said Leo. Tom tied the flag to the stick and held it up high.
Lily, Mia, and Leo smiled and clapped. The paw print was white on the green cloth. Pip sat on the grass with his red ball and watched the flag. "Woof!" said Pip.
text.summary: Leo wants to paint a flag for the club. Pip steps in the white paint and jumps on the cloth, and his paw print becomes the club sign.

Lily and Mia sat on the grass and watched him.

"I want to paint a white leaf in the middle," said Leo.
"A leaf is a nice design," said Mia.
"Wait here, please," said Leo.
"I need a drink first."
He left the pot and the brush beside the cloth and went into the house.
Pip played near the gate with his red ball.
Then the ball went across the grass.
Pip was running after his red ball when he stepped in the pot of paint.
His front paws were white and wet.
"Pip!" shouted Lily.
Leo was coming back with a cup of water when Pip suddenly jumped on the cloth.

His white paws were still wet.
Lily and Mia began to laugh.
"It looks like a paw print," said Lily.
"Pip made a special sign for the club by accident!"
"A paw print on a green flag is perfect," said Mia.

Then he began to smile.

Leo decided to keep it.
They waited in the sun for an hour.
Lily's brother Tom came out of the house with a long stick.

Tom tied the flag to the stick and held it up high.
Lily, Mia, and Leo smiled and clapped.
The paw print was white on the green cloth.
Pip sat on the grass with his red ball and watched the flag.
"Woof!" said Pip.
